card: Expands the IPC fuzz target to test bidirectional callback communication, server-side argument integrity, and client/server deserialization of arbitrary raw transaction and UniValue payloads. The change ensures libmultiprocess and its Cap'n Proto hooks handle malformed inputs gracefully without relying solely on valid round-trip serialization. It builds on #35118 and contributes toward multiprocess fuzzing goals in #23015.
changed_since_previous: Patch-id updated from cbcf35a3ec5185bc to 3dc8ba294e6b45da, but the overall approach, commit structure, and modified files remain unchanged.
evidence: Follows up on merged PR #35118 and implements reviewer suggestions to assert arguments on the server side (PR description citing reviews on #35118).
Continues implementation of the IPC fuzzing proposal outlined in open issue #23015.
problem: The existing IPC fuzz target only tested round-trip calls using valid data generated by libmultiprocess serialization, leaving reverse callback communication, server-side deserialization discrepancies, and parser handling of raw or malformed payloads unexercised.

risk.why: Modifications are restricted entirely to IPC fuzz test targets and will not impact production node behavior or release binaries.

scope_notes: Touches only fuzz testing code under `src/ipc/test/fuzz/` without changing production IPC or libmultiprocess logic.
summary: Expands the `ipc` fuzz target to exercise bidirectional IPC callbacks and inject arbitrary Cap'n Proto payloads for `CTransaction` and `UniValue` types. It also adds server-side assertions to ensure deserialized arguments match sent values prior to round-trip return.
